name: Question 1
problem:
The triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={\int }_{a}^{b}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}{\int }_{∗}^{∗}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz
$$

is defined over the type II region $R,$ given by

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,-8\le y\le {sin}^{2}⁡z,\,0\le z\le \pi ,\,-2y-1\le x\le {y}^{2}+2z}.
$$

What is $a+b?$
worked_solution:
A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,{u}_{1}(y,z)\le x\le {u}_{2}(y,z)}.
$$

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063435/assets/a905e1f60fb0aa865c071fcbccbfecb30dcac7a74b4b647d24a40f4c89ff1935.png)

 

If $R$ is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of $f(x,y,z)$ over $R$ as a mixed integral, as follows:

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{{u}_{1}(y,z)}^{{u}_{2}(y,z)}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}x]\,\text{d}A
$$

In our case, we have

$$
{u}_{1}(y,z)=-2y-1,\,{u}_{2}(y,z)={y}^{2}+2z.
$$

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,\text{d}V={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA.
$$

Now, the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-8\le y\le {sin}^{2}⁡z,\,0\le z\le \pi }.
$$

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over $D$ as a repeated integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dA & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{-8}^{{sin}^{2}⁡z}[{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx]dy\,\text{d}z \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{-8}^{{sin}^{2}⁡z}{\int }_{-2y-1}^{{y}^{2}+2z}f(x,y,z)\,dx\,dy\,dz.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=0+\pi =\pi .
$$

Question 1
?

The triple integral ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∫ab∫∗∗∫∗∗f(x,y,z)dxdydz is defined over the type II region R, given by R={(x,y,z):−8≤y≤sin2⁡z,0≤z≤π,−2y−1≤x≤y2+2z}. What is a+b?

a
sin2⁡z+π−8
b
sin2⁡z−8
c
y2+2z−2y−1
d
y2+2z−2y
e
π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

A type II region in three-dimensional space can be written as

R={(x,y,z):(y,z)∈D,u1(y,z)≤x≤u2(y,z)}.

A typical three-dimensional type II region can be visualized schematically, as shown below.

If R is a type II region, we can express the triple integral of f(x,y,z) over R as a mixed integral, as follows:

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫u1(y,z)u2(y,z)f(x,y,z)dx]dA

In our case, we have

u1(y,z)=−2y−1,u2(y,z)=y2+2z.

Therefore, our triple integral can be written as ∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∬D[∫−2y−1y2+2zf(x,y,z)dx]dA.

Now, the region D is given by D={(x,y):−8≤y≤sin2⁡z,0≤z≤π}.

Therefore, by expressing the double integral over D as a repeated integral, we get ∬D[∫−2y−1y2+2zf(x,y,z)dx]dA=∫0π∫−8sin2⁡z[∫−2y−1y2+2zf(x,y,z)dx]dydz=∫0π∫−8sin2⁡z∫−2y−1y2+2zf(x,y,z)dxdydz.

Finally, a+b=0+π=π.
